title: Viajar
goal: Get through the airport, check into a hotel, get around, and start telling por from para.

lessons.title: At the airport
lessons.notes:
Airport words, Latin American style:
**el boleto** is a ticket (Spain: **el billete**; also **el pasaje** in much of South America).
**la salida** is both departure and the way out; **la llegada** is arrival (from **llegar**).
When you check in your bag, you'll hear **documentar** in Mexico and **facturar** in Spain - both fine to recognise.
**¿A qué hora sale el vuelo?** = What time does the flight leave? **salir** is the verb for planes, trains and buses leaving.

sentences.es: ¿A qué hora sale el vuelo?
sentences.en: What time does the flight leave?
accept_en: What time does the flight depart?

sentences.es: Necesito el pasaporte y el boleto.
sentences.en: I need my passport and ticket.
accept_en: I need the passport and the ticket.
I need my passport and my ticket.

sentences.es: Mi maleta es muy grande.
sentences.en: My suitcase is very big.

sentences.es: Llegamos al aeropuerto a las seis.
sentences.en: We arrived at the airport at six.
accept_en: We get to the airport at six.
We arrive at the airport at six.

sentences.es: El avión llega una hora tarde.
sentences.en: The plane is arriving an hour late.
accept_en: The plane arrives an hour late.
The plane is an hour late.
The plane is one hour late.

sentences.es: ¿Dónde está la salida?
sentences.en: Where is the exit?

sentences.es: La llegada es a las diez de la noche.
sentences.en: The arrival is at ten at night.
accept_en: We arrive at ten at night.

sentences.es: ¿Cómo fue el viaje?
sentences.en: How was the trip?

sentences.es: ¡Buen viaje! ¡Hasta pronto!
sentences.en: Have a good trip! See you soon!
accept_en: Have a nice trip! See you soon!

lessons.title: At the hotel
lessons.notes:
Checking in: **Tengo una reservación a nombre de...** = I have a booking under the name... (Spain: **una reserva**).
Rooms: **una habitación sencilla** (single; Spain: **individual**) or **doble**.
The lift is **el elevador** in much of Latin America and **el ascensor** in Spain and the Southern Cone - you'll hear both.
**¿Está incluido el desayuno?** = Is breakfast included? **incluido** agrees: **la cena está incluida**.
Ask politely with **¿Me puede...?** (Can you... for me?): **¿Me puede dar la llave?**

sentences.es: Tengo una reservación a nombre de Pérez.
sentences.en: I have a booking under the name Pérez.
accept_en: I have a reservation in the name of Pérez.
I've got a booking under Pérez.

sentences.es: Quisiera una habitación doble, por favor.
sentences.en: I'd like a double room, please.

sentences.es: Reservé una habitación sencilla para dos noches.
sentences.en: I booked a single room for two nights.
accept_en: I reserved a single room for two nights.
I've booked a single room for two nights.

sentences.es: ¿Está incluido el desayuno?
sentences.en: Is breakfast included?

sentences.es: ¿Me puede dar la llave, por favor?
sentences.en: Can you give me the key, please?
accept_en: Could you give me the key, please?
Can I have the key, please?

sentences.es: La habitación está en el piso cinco.
sentences.en: The room is on floor five.
accept_en: The room is on the fifth floor.

sentences.es: El elevador está a la derecha.
sentences.en: The lift is on the right.
accept_en: The elevator is on the right.
The lift is to the right.

sentences.es: Quiero reservar una mesa para cuatro.
sentences.en: I want to book a table for four.
accept_en: I'd like to book a table for four.
I want to reserve a table for four.

lessons.title: Getting around
lessons.notes:
In Latin America you **tomar** a bus or train: **tomar el autobús**. Spain says **coger el autobús** - avoid coger in much of Latin America, where it's rude!
The bus has many names: **el autobús** is understood everywhere; you'll also hear **el camión** (Mexico), **la micro** (Chile), **el colectivo** (Argentina).
Tickets: **de ida** (one way), **de ida y vuelta** (return).
Getting lost: **perderse** (e -> ie): **Me perdí.** = I got lost.
To ask the way: **¿Cómo llego a...?** = How do I get to...?

items.note: e -> ie: me pierdo. Preterite: me perdí.

sentences.es: Tomamos el tren a las ocho.
sentences.en: We take the train at eight.
accept_en: We took the train at eight.
We catch the train at eight.

sentences.es: ¿Dónde está la estación de autobuses?
sentences.en: Where is the bus station?

sentences.es: Un boleto de ida y vuelta, por favor.
sentences.en: A return ticket, please.

sentences.es: Solo quiero un boleto de ida.
sentences.en: I only want a one-way ticket.
accept_en: I just want a one-way ticket.
I only want a single ticket.

sentences.es: Ayer me perdí en el centro.
sentences.en: Yesterday I got lost in the city centre.
accept_en: I got lost in the centre yesterday.
Yesterday I got lost in the centre.

sentences.es: Perdón, ¿cómo llego al museo?
sentences.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?
accept_en: Sorry, how do I get to the museum?

sentences.es: Sin mapa, siempre me pierdo.
sentences.en: Without a map, I always get lost.
accept_en: I always get lost without a map.

sentences.es: Tomamos un taxi porque llovía.
sentences.en: We took a taxi because it was raining.
accept_en: We took a cab because it was raining.
We got a taxi because it was raining.

sentences.es: El autobús llegó muy tarde.
sentences.en: The bus arrived very late.

lessons.title: Por or para?
lessons.notes:
Both often mean "for", but they look in different directions.
**para** points **forward**, to a goal:
- purpose: **para** + infinitive = in order to: **Estudio para viajar.**
- destination: **El tren para Lima.**
- recipient: **Es para ti.** (It's for you.)
- deadline: **para el lunes**
**por** looks at the **route or the cause**:
- through / around: **Caminamos por la ciudad.**
- because of / thanks for: **Gracias por todo.**
- by means of: **por teléfono**
- exchange: **Pagué cien dólares por el boleto.**
- time of day: **por la mañana**
Rule of thumb: goal -> **para**; reason, route, swap -> **por**.

sentences.es: Estudio español para viajar por Sudamérica.
sentences.en: I'm studying Spanish to travel around South America.
accept_en: I study Spanish to travel around South America.
I study Spanish in order to travel through South America.

sentences.es: Este regalo es para ti.
sentences.en: This present is for you.

sentences.es: Gracias por todo.
sentences.en: Thanks for everything.

sentences.es: Reservé el hotel por teléfono.
sentences.en: I booked the hotel by phone.
accept_en: I booked the hotel over the phone.
I reserved the hotel by phone.

sentences.es: ¿Hay una farmacia por aquí?
sentences.en: Is there a chemist around here?
accept_en: Is there a pharmacy near here?
Is there a chemist near here?
Is there a pharmacy around here?

sentences.es: Pagué cincuenta dólares por la habitación.
sentences.en: I paid fifty dollars for the room.

sentences.es: Necesito el boleto para el lunes.
sentences.en: I need the ticket by Monday.
accept_en: I need the ticket for Monday.

sentences.es: Caminamos por la playa por la tarde.
sentences.en: We walked along the beach in the afternoon.
accept_en: We walk along the beach in the afternoon.
We walked on the beach in the afternoon.
We walked along the beach in the evening.

sentences.es: El año pasado fuimos de vacaciones a otro país.
sentences.en: Last year we went on holiday to another country.
accept_en: Last year we went on vacation to another country.
Last year we went to another country on holiday.
